Japan was the only country with which India had both an Annual Summit and a 2+2 ministerial mechanism; the first 2+2 was held in 2019.
RPSS between Japan's Self-Defense Forces and Indian Armed Forces was signed on 9 September 2020.
India-Japan ties have more than 70 bilateral dialogue mechanisms across sectors.
Indian monk Bodhisena consecrated the Great Buddha at Todaiji Temple, Nara, in 752 AD.

mains.text: RPSS covers supplies and services during bilateral training, UN peacekeeping and humanitarian relief, and raises interoperability.
Japan joined the multilateral exercise MILAN for the first time, and RPSS was operationalised in March 2022.
The 2022 Tokyo 2+2 marked 70 years of India-Japan diplomatic relations.
Leaders reaffirmed a free and open Indo-Pacific underpinned by inclusiveness and rules-based order as the basis of cooperation.

prelims.text: ICJ has 15 judges elected for nine-year terms by the UN General Assembly and Security Council; seat at the Peace Palace, The Hague.
The Genocide Convention was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 9 December 1948.
The Gambia filed the case on 11 November 2019, on behalf of the 57-member OIC.
Jurisdiction rests on Article IX of the Genocide Convention; ICJ upheld it on 22 July 2022.
ICJ, the UN's principal judicial organ, was established by the UN Charter in June 1945.

mains.text: ICJ (19 November 2026) found Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during 2017 'clearance operations'.
Article 9 of the Genocide Convention lets parties take disputes on a State's responsibility for genocide to the ICJ.
ICJ ordered provisional measures against Myanmar on 23 January 2020, before the merits stage.
Reparation will be fixed later; Myanmar must report to the Court within two years of the judgment.

prelims.text: EPFO, an autonomous body under the Labour Ministry, administers the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and its schemes.
Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 came into force on 16 November 1995 under Section 6A of the 1952 Act.
EPS is funded by 8.33% of wages from the employer's share and 1.16% by the Central Government, subject to wage ceiling.
EPS 1995 replaced the Employees' Family Pension Scheme, 1971.
CBT recommended 8.25% interest on EPF accumulations for 2025-26.

mains.text: Three schemes run under the 1952 Act: EPF Scheme 1952, EPS 1995 and EDLI Scheme 1976.
Section 10 of the EPF & MP Act protects provident fund money from attachment by any court.
CPPS for EPS 1995 disbursed about ₹1,612 crore to more than 69 lakh pensioners in February 2025.
Membership continues to age 58; pension covers superannuation, early retirement, disability and family pension, so phased payouts can extend income security.

prelims.text: LARR Act is Act No. 30 of 2013, dated 26 September 2013; it replaced the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
Consent needed: 80% of affected families for private companies, 70% for PPP; none for government projects.
Section 41(3): acquisition in Scheduled Areas needs prior consent of the Gram Sabha, Panchayats or autonomous District Councils.
Compensation is up to four times market value in rural areas and twice in urban areas.
Every acquisition requires a Social Impact Assessment and rehabilitation and resettlement for those affected.

mains.text: The Act seeks a humane, participative, informed and transparent acquisition process in consultation with local self-government and Gram Sabhas.
Sections 41 and 42 add special safeguards against displacement for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The 2015 amendment Bill sought to exempt defence, rural infrastructure, affordable housing, industrial corridors and PPP infrastructure from SIA and consent.
PRS noted the five exempted categories are broad; keep SIA and consent as the default for public-purpose projects.

prelims.text: Updated NDC (August 2022): cut emissions intensity of GDP 45% by 2030 from 2005 level.
NDC also targets about 50% cumulative installed power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030.
India's Panchamrit pledges at COP26, Glasgow included net-zero emissions by 2070.
India submitted its first NDC on 2 October 2015.
COP28 in Dubai (30 November-13 December 2023) adopted the outcome of the first Global Stocktake.

mains.text: India adheres to Equity and Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) under UNFCCC.
By June 2025 India had reduced emissions intensity of GDP by around 36% from 2005.
India's NDC includes the LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) mass movement as key to combating climate change.
India links its 50% non-fossil target to technology transfer and low-cost international finance, including from the Green Climate Fund.

prelims.text: NCMM was approved on 29 January 2025: ₹16,300 crore expenditure plus ₹18,000 crore expected from PSUs, total ₹34,300 crore.
NCMM runs seven years, 2024-25 to 2030-31.
A November 2022 Mines Ministry committee identified 30 critical minerals; 24 are in Part D of Schedule I of the MMDR Act.
MMDR Act was amended in 2023 to boost exploration and mining of critical minerals.
KABIL, a Mines Ministry JV, acquired about 15,703 ha in Catamarca, Argentina, for lithium exploration.

mains.text: NCMM covers the whole value chain: exploration, mining, beneficiation, processing and recovery from end-of-life products.
GSI is tasked with 1,200 exploration projects from 2024-25 to 2030-31 under the Mission.
Ministry of Mines has auctioned 34 critical mineral blocks.
NCMM aims at fast-track approvals, incentives for exploration and recovery from overburden and tailings.

prelims.text: First NAP-AMR was launched on 19 April 2017, aligned with WHO's Global Action Plan, for 2017-2021.
NAP-AMR 2.0 covers 2025-2029 with a One Health approach.
Schedule H1 (from March 2014) covers about 24 third/fourth-generation cephalosporins and carbapenems; sale needs a prescription.
NARS-Net, a network of State medical college labs, generates AMR data on priority bacterial pathogens.
The Delhi Declaration on AMR was signed by ministers of four ministries at the 2017 launch.

mains.text: AMR needs a One Health approach coordinating human, animal, agriculture and environment sectors.
COVID-19 stalled implementation of the first NAP-AMR during 2020-22.
Under India's G20 presidency in 2023, AMR featured in the Leaders' Declaration.
CDSCO enforcement drives on Schedule H and H1 must continue; each sector must commit under NAP-AMR 2.0.

prelims.text: ULLAS (New India Literacy Programme) is a centrally sponsored scheme for FYs 2022-27, targeting non-literates aged 15 and above.
Its outlay is ₹1,037.90 crore for 2022-23 to 2026-27.
Five components: Foundational Literacy and Numeracy, Critical Life Skills, Basic Education, Vocational Skills, Continuing Education.
Education Ministry treats 95% literacy in a State/UT as equivalent to full literacy.
Ladakh was declared fully functionally literate on 24 June 2024, the first such administrative unit.

mains.text: Literacy is defined as the ability to read, write and compute with comprehension, plus critical life skills such as digital and financial literacy.
Ten States/UTs declared themselves fully literate between 2024 and 2026, including Mizoram, Goa, Tripura and Himachal Pradesh.
Tripura became fully literate at 95.6%, up from 20.24% in 1961.
The scheme runs on volunteerism with content in local languages; sustain it towards full literacy by 2030 under NEP 2020.

prelims.text: Project components: 14.2 million TEU transhipment terminal, greenfield airport (4,000 peak-hour passengers), 450 MVA gas-solar plant and a township.
Galathea Bay port lies about 40 nautical miles from the East-West shipping route, with natural depth over 20 metres.
The proposed township spans 16,610 hectares.
ICTP project cost was put at ₹44,313 crore in PM GatiShakti Network Planning Group evaluation.
ICTP is a key project under Maritime India Vision 2030 and Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.

mains.text: Government says no displacement is proposed for Shompen and Nicobarese and notified tribal reserve area will rise through re-notification.
The project aims to reduce dependence on foreign transhipment ports and serve defence and national security purposes.
Government FAQ: project strengthens India's presence in the Andaman Sea and Southeast Asia and integrates the island with global trade.
Government FAQ says PVTGs, especially Shompen, must not be adversely affected; FRA consent processes need verifiable compliance.

prelims.text: The new ICI series has base year 2022-23; weights derive from the IIP (2022-23) and are scaled to 100.
Electricity weight rose from 19.853% to 30.932% in the 2022-23 ICI series.
Iron ore was added to the ICI basket in the 2022-23 series with a 4.905% weight.
In the 2011-12 series, refinery products had the highest weight at 28.04%.
In the 2011-12 series, eight core industries were 40.27% of IIP item weights.

mains.text: Only raw coal is retained in the new ICI series; coal middlings and washed coal are dropped to avoid double counting.
Electricity weight rose due to higher GVA of the sector from 2011-12 to 2022-23 and inclusion of renewable sources.
First press release of the 2022-23 ICI series gives refinery products 22.572 and steel 17.584 weights.
ICI measures production of eight core industries only, so a low base or one sector can drive headline growth.

prelims.text: Parliament enacted the ISRWD Act, 1956 under Article 262; it was last amended in August 2002.
Cauvery Water Management Scheme was notified on 1 June 2018, constituting CWMA and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee.
SC (February 2018) cut Karnataka's normal-year delivery to Tamil Nadu at Biligundlu from 192 TMC to 177.25 TMC.
Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted on 2 June 1990.
A Tribunal decision, once published, has the same force as an order or decree of the Supreme Court (Section 6(2)).

mains.text: Article 262 lets Parliament bar the Supreme Court and other courts from inter-State river water disputes.
The CWDT award merged with the SC judgment of 16 February 2018, and the CWDT was dissolved.
In 2023 the SC declined to interfere with CWRC and CWMA release orders, noting they consist of water and agriculture experts.
CWMA has powers over storage, apportionment and regulation to secure compliance with the modified award; States should use it before courts.

prelims.text: 42nd Amendment (1976) froze each State's Lok Sabha and Assembly seats on the 1971 census until the first census after 2000.
84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze until the first census after 2026.
The last Delimitation Commission was set up in 2002 and its orders were finalised in 2008.
The 2002 Commission, chaired by Justice Kuldip Singh, began functioning on 4 July 2002.
Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 16 April 2026.

mains.text: Under Article 82, Parliament enacts a Delimitation Act after every census; the Centre then constitutes a Delimitation Commission.
Delimitation Bill, 2026 uses the latest published census when the Commission is constituted, implying the 2011 census.
Home Minister: with seats frozen since 1971, 127 constituencies have more than 20 lakh voters each.
The 2001 freeze was a motivational measure so States could pursue population stabilisation; population-only seats could penalise them.

prelims.text: WHO (April 2015): population-level C-section rates above 10% are not associated with lower maternal and newborn mortality.
About 15% of pregnancies are assumed to develop complications requiring surgical intervention.
Institutional births rose from 79% (NFHS-4) to 89% (NFHS-5).
NFHS-6 (2023-24): institutional deliveries rose from 88.6% to 90.6%.
NFHS-4 Delhi: C-sections were 42.9% of births in private facilities versus 21% in public ones.

mains.text: IIT Madras study: private-sector C-section share rose from 43.1% (2016) to 49.7% (2021), nearly one in two deliveries.
IIT Madras found place of delivery mattered most, implying clinical need was not necessarily the reason for surgical deliveries.
NFHS-5 recorded a substantial rise in C-section deliveries in many States, especially in private facilities.
Caesarean section is life-saving when needed but carries inherent surgical risks; audit private-sector rates against clinical indications.

prelims.text: MHA is the nodal Ministry and Central Authority for seeking and giving mutual legal assistance in criminal matters.
MHA's IS-II Division handles mutual legal assistance in criminal matters.
Section 105 CrPC provides for reciprocal arrangements with foreign governments on service of summons and judicial processes.
India had MLATs or agreements with 42 countries and is party to UNCAC and UNTOC (2020).
MHA's International Cooperation Division negotiates MLATs and security cooperation agreements.

mains.text: Assistance is sought through MLA requests, letters rogatory, and service of summons on persons residing abroad.
India-US MLAT requires assistance whether or not the conduct is an offence under the requested State's law.
MHA guidelines set service of documents abroad preferably within 10 days for offences against women and children.
MHA runs mutual legal assistance training for investigators, prosecutors and judicial officers; expand it to cut delays.

prelims.text: Cosmetics are regulated under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Cosmetics Rules, 2020.
Cosmetics Rules, 2020 were notified by GSR 763(E) dated 15 December 2020.
State Licensing Authorities license cosmetic manufacture; the DCGI, as Central Licensing Authority, registers imports.
Drugs and Cosmetics Rules prohibit cosmetics containing mercury compounds and lead or arsenic compounds for colouring.
BIS standards set maximum limits of 20 ppm for lead and 2 ppm for arsenic in cosmetics.

mains.text: Section 3(aaa) of the 1940 Act defines a cosmetic as an article applied to the body for cleansing, beautifying or altering appearance.
Section 10 bars import of cosmetics that are not of standard quality, or are misbranded or spurious.
CDSCO lists heavy-metal test reports for mercury, lead and arsenic that do not meet Cosmetics Rules limits as a common non-compliance.
Import registration requires a declaration on heavy metal and hexachlorophene content; extend similar scrutiny to products sold online.

prelims.text: India was re-elected to the IMO Council in Category B, the 10 States with the largest interest in seaborne trade, for 2026-27.
India topped Category B with 154 of 169 valid votes at the 34th IMO Assembly on 28 November 2025.
The IMO Council has 40 members: 10 each in Categories A and B and 20 in Category C.
India has served on the IMO Council since it began functioning, except during 1983-1984.
India is a founder member of the IMO, the UN specialised agency on maritime safety and marine environment protection.

mains.text: India's Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines (2023) set a roadmap to cut carbon intensity at major ports.
Green Tug Transition Programme (2024) and Harit Nauka initiative promote low-emission, alternative-fuel vessels.
India has more than 145,000 active seafarers, giving it a large stake in global shipping rules.
Minister: green hydrogen, ammonia, biofuels and LNG are the future of maritime fuels; India can supply green fuels to global shipping.

prelims.text: The CCW was negotiated under UN auspices in 1979-1980 and rests on IHL principles such as proportionality and distinction.
The first formal meeting of the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS was held in Geneva, 13-17 November 2017.
India's Ambassador Amandeep Singh Gill chaired the GGE on LAWS in 2017-2018.
The GGE adopts its report by consensus and submits it to the Meeting of High Contracting Parties to the CCW.
The GGE on LAWS was established by Decision 1 of the Fifth CCW Review Conference.

mains.text: India addresses LAWS within the CCW framework, which balances military necessity with humanitarian considerations.
India holds that emerging technologies could, in general, improve compliance with international humanitarian law.
Several States told the UN Secretary-General that the GGE balances humanitarian concerns with legitimate self-defence interests.
Many States see the CCW structure, which allows new protocols, as suited to address emerging weapons technologies.

prelims.text: DBT created BRIC on 10 November 2023, with Cabinet approval, by subsuming 14 autonomous institutions.
BRIC is an apex autonomous body registered as a Society under the Ministry of Science and Technology.
BRIC-NABI, Mohali merged NABI and the Centre of Innovative and Applied Bioprocessing (CIAB).
BRIC's Research Advisory Board is chaired by Prof. K. VijayRaghavan, former Principal Scientific Adviser.
The DBT Secretary also serves as Director General of BRIC.

mains.text: BRIC aims at centralised, unified governance to maximise the impact of biotech research.
BRIC institutes retain distinct research identities; three DBT-BRIC researchers ran experiments on the ISS in the Axiom-4 mission.
DBT set up India's first National Biofoundry Network to strengthen indigenous biomanufacturing.
Government says BRIC should scale biotech research for Atmanirbhar Bharat in healthcare, food and energy.

prelims.text: Movement across the India-Nepal border is governed by the Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950, which allows free movement of citizens.
Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) is the border guarding force on the India-Nepal border.
Nepal borders five Indian States: Sikkim, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
About 32,000 Gorkha soldiers from Nepal serve in the Indian Army.
India and Nepal signed a Treaty of Trade and Commerce at Kathmandu on 31 July 1950.

mains.text: India is Nepal's largest trade partner; bilateral trade crossed USD 7 billion in 2019-20, and India transits almost all Nepal's third-country trade.
India handed over 50,000 reconstructed houses in Gorkha and Nuwakot districts on 15 November 2021 (USD 150 million aid).
Demarcation of Kalapani and Susta is incomplete; Kalapani decides the India-Nepal-China tri-junction.
Use the more than 40 bilateral mechanisms, including the Joint Commission, on border, power, water and railways.

prelims.text: India and China agreed in 2003 to appoint Special Representatives on the boundary question; 24 rounds held by August 2025.
WMCC was set up by an agreement signed at the 15th round of SR talks, New Delhi, January 2012.
A 2005 protocol set modalities for confidence building measures along the LAC.
India and China agreed on patrolling arrangements in Depsang and Demchok on 21 October 2024, leading to disengagement.
On 1 April 1950, India became the first non-socialist bloc country to establish relations with the PRC.

mains.text: There is no commonly delineated LAC; differing perceptions lead to transgressions when both sides patrol up to their claims.
Defence Ministry: in 2025 PLA kept 10 Combined Arms Brigade-size forces opposite the Northern borders.
Transgressions are taken up via border personnel meetings, flag meetings, WMCC and diplomatic channels.
Both sides agreed to pursue disengagement, de-escalation, border management and eventual delimitation through existing mechanisms.

prelims.text: TRISHNA (Thermal Infra-Red Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural resource Assessment) is a joint ISRO-CNES mission.
CNES provides TRISHNA's thermal infrared payload, a four-channel long-wave infrared imaging sensor.
TRISHNA will offer 60 m spatial resolution with a 3-day revisit at the equator, for 5 years with a possible 2-year extension.
Joint ISRO-CNES satellites Megha-Tropiques and SARAL were launched on PSLV-C18 (2011) and PSLV-C20 (2013).
Megha-Tropiques studies the water cycle in the tropical atmosphere; the ISRO-CNES MoU was signed in May 2001.

mains.text: India-France Joint Vision for Space Cooperation (March 2018) covers climate monitoring, TRISHNA and space situational awareness.
TRISHNA will monitor crop water stress, irrigation needs, water resources, urban ecosystems and glaciers.
Cooperation includes NavIC ground station development in France and French support for Gaganyaan.
India and France commemorated 50 years of space cooperation with joint stamps; expand into earth observation, launch and exploration.

prelims.text: Article 85(1): the President summons each House, but six months shall not intervene between two sessions.
Article 85(2): the President may prorogue the Houses or either House and dissolve the Lok Sabha.
Article 196(3): a Bill pending in a State Legislature does not lapse on prorogation.
The Government of India Act, 1935 also provided that a pending Bill would not lapse on prorogation of the Chambers.
The Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs decides on convening Parliament; the President formalises it.

mains.text: Article 85 is based on the Government of India Act, 1935, which required a session at least once in 12 months.
Ambedkar's draft reduced the gap between sessions to six months and required Parliament to meet at least twice a year.
The Constituent Assembly rejected letting the Speaker or Chairman summon the House if the President failed to.
The power to convene Parliament rests with the government; a fixed calendar would limit this executive discretion.

prelims.text: VVP-I was approved on 15 February 2023 for villages in 46 blocks of 19 northern border districts in four States and Ladakh.
VVP-I outlay is ₹4,800 crore for 2022-23 to 2025-26, of which ₹2,500 crore is for all-weather roads.
VVP was launched from Kibithoo village in Anjaw district, Arunachal Pradesh, on 10 April 2023.
VVP-II, a Central Sector Scheme with ₹6,839 crore to 2028-29, covers villages on other international land borders.
Arunachal Pradesh has 455 of the villages identified under VVP-I, the most of any State.

mains.text: VVP-I and VVP-II together have a combined outlay of ₹11,639 crore.
VVP focuses on livelihoods through tourism, cultural heritage, skill development, entrepreneurship and cooperatives.
Under VVP-I, 263 tourism projects worth ₹116 crore were approved, including viewpoints and eco-tourism.
Government frames border villages as strategic partners in security; sustain roads, power, telecom and livelihoods to retain residents.

prelims.text: The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (No. 34 of 2006) received assent on 23 August 2006.
FSSAI was established under Section 4 of the Act by notification dated 5 September 2008.
FSS regulations cap bromates in packaged drinking water at 0.01 mg/l.
Packaged drinking water is certified by BIS under IS 14543, with bromate tested once in six months.
Composition of the Food Authority is prescribed in Section 5 of the FSS Act.

mains.text: The FSS Act consolidated food laws to create a single statutory body for standard setting and enforcement.
The Act moved from a multi-level, multi-departmental system to a single line of command on food safety.
FSSAI found packaged water makers running with an FSSAI licence but no BIS mark, or vice versa, and ordered surveillance.
FSSAI directed State food safety departments to run regular enforcement and surveillance of packaged water makers.

prelims.text: Renaming a State needs Parliament's approval under Articles 3 and 4; the President refers the Bill to the State legislature for its views.
The Orissa Assembly resolved on 28 August 2008 to rename the State Odisha; the Bill passed Rajya Sabha on 24 March 2011.
The Uttaranchal (Alteration of Name) Act, 2006 (No. 52 of 2006) renamed the State Uttarakhand.
Kerala Assembly passed a resolution on 24 June 2024 to rename the State 'Keralam'.
The Orissa renaming also changed the language name from Oriya to Odia, via the Constitution (113th Amendment) Bill.

mains.text: A renaming Bill amends the State's entry in the First Schedule to the Constitution.
The Uttaranchal Act also amended the Fourth Schedule, which allots Rajya Sabha seats, to reflect the new name.
For Keralam, the Union Cabinet approved a Bill which the President refers to the Kerala Assembly under the proviso to Article 3.
Kerala's resolution tied its name to Malayalam and linguistic State formation on 1 November 1956; renaming should follow such clear State consensus.

prelims.text: GSI is the nodal agency for landslide studies and completed NLSM mapping at 1:50,000 scale over about 4.3 lakh sq km in 19 States/UTs.
The NLSM programme was launched in 2014-15 by GSI under the Ministry of Mines.
NLSM was formally launched on 5 February 2014 at the 53rd Central Geological Programming Board meeting.
Landslide-prone hilly terrain in parts of 19 States/UTs affects parts of 179 districts.
The National Landslide Forecasting Centre (NLFC) of GSI issues landslide forecast bulletins on its Bhusanket portal.

mains.text: NDMA, with GSI, framed the National Landslide Risk Management Strategy (NLRMS) in 2019.
Susceptibility maps classify areas into high, moderate and low zones by likelihood of landslide initiation.
GSI had inventoried 87,474 active landslides alongside the baseline susceptibility maps.
GSI aims to develop an easy-to-use, effective landslide early warning system (LEWS) to reduce losses.

prelims.text: NDMA issued Guidelines on Management of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) in October 2020.
NGRMP covers Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Uttarakhand with ₹150 crore outlay.
CWC monitors 477 Himalayan glacial lakes and water bodies over 50 hectares monthly in the monsoon since 2011.
NDMA's Committee on Disaster Risk Reduction (CoDRR), with six Himalayan States/UTs, identified high-risk glacial lakes for expeditions.
Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology monitors glaciers and analyses hazard triggers.

mains.text: Central Electricity Authority identified 47 dams likely to be affected by GLOFs from Indian glacial lakes.
NGRMP builds a glacial lake inventory, early warning systems and automatic weather stations for real-time monitoring.
NRSC and CWC inventories support mitigation such as de-watering and controlled breaching of risky lakes.
NDMA's GLOF SOP covers pre-disaster preparedness, real-time response and recovery; apply it to works near high-risk lakes.

prelims.text: Section 2(2) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 says the Act does not apply to members of Scheduled Tribes.
SC (2022): denying succession to ST women would deprive them of the right to livelihood under Article 21.
SC asked the Central Government to consider withdrawing the HSA exemption for Scheduled Tribes.
SC (2025 INSC 865) heard a Gond woman's heirs claiming an equal share in her father's property.
SC (2024 INSC 1005) directed the Centre to examine withdrawing the HSA exemption for Scheduled Tribes.

mains.text: SC (Madhu Kishwar case): excluding tribal women from inheritance under customary law, based solely on sex, is discriminatory.
In the 2022 case an ST daughter claimed a share of land acquisition compensation; respondents cited Section 2(2).
Courts deny claims where plaintiffs fail to prove community custom granting daughters rights.
SC directed the Centre to decide whether to amend the HSA to cover Scheduled Tribes.

prelims.text: INS Arnala, the first of sixteen ASW-SWC ships, was commissioned at Visakhapatnam on 18 June 2025.
GRSE builds eight ASW SWCs; Arnala was built under a PPP with L&T Shipbuilders, Kattupalli.
Arnala-class ships replace the Abhay-class ASW corvettes.
INS Arnala is 77 m long, the largest naval warship propelled by a diesel engine-waterjet combination.
ASW SWCs carry over 80% indigenous content.

mains.text: The ships do sub-surface surveillance, search and rescue, Low Intensity Maritime Operations and mine laying in littoral waters.
Sensors include hull-mounted sonar and Low Frequency Variable Depth Sonar, with torpedoes, ASW rockets and NSG-30 gun.
INS Arnala, Androth and Mahe were inducted in 2025, part of the Navy's Aatmanirbhar journey.
Armed forces have identified over 5,000 items to source domestically; extend this to sonars and weapons.

prelims.text: RBI issued the D-SIB framework on 22 July 2014, updated on 28 December 2023.
2025 list: SBI in Bucket 4 (0.80% of RWAs), HDFC Bank in Bucket 2 (0.40%), ICICI Bank in Bucket 1 (0.20%).
The additional CET1 requirement applies over and above the capital conservation buffer.
Five buckets: 0.20% to 1.00% of RWAs; Bucket 5 (1%) is kept empty as a deterrent against rising scores.
Indicators: size (40% weight), interconnectedness, substitutability and complexity (20% each).
Banks with size above 2% of GDP (Basel III leverage-ratio exposure) form the assessment sample.

mains.text: The framework follows BCBS methodology; G20 leaders in November 2011 asked BCBS and FSB to extend the G-SIB framework to D-SIBs.
A foreign G-SIB branch in India keeps a surcharge proportionate to its India share of global RWAs.
SBI moved from Bucket 3 to 4 and HDFC Bank from 1 to 2 in the 2023 list, effective 1 April 2025.
D-SIBs face more intensive supervision and must keep sound risk governance; RBI reviews the methodology at least every three years.
RBI's 2013 FSR noted the top five banks held about 35% of assets, so too-big-to-fail was less critical in India.

prelims.text: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 is India's first dedicated law against paper leaks and organised exam fraud.
It covers exams of UPSC, SSC, RRBs, IBPS, NTA and Central Ministries/Departments for recruitment.
Unfair means include leaking a question paper or answer key and tampering with computer resources.
Organised exam crime (Section 11) carries 5-10 years' jail and a fine of at least ₹1 crore.
An errant service provider faces a fine up to ₹1 crore and a four-year ban from conducting public exams.
The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 27 July 2026.

mains.text: The 2026 Bill raises the organised-crime minimum to 7 years and ₹10 crore, and the service-provider fine to ₹5 crore.
For individual offenders, the Bill raises punishment from 3-5 years and ₹10 lakh to 5-10 years and up to ₹50 lakh.
NEET 2026 was cancelled in May 2026 after an alleged paper leak and re-conducted the next month.
States legislate too: Bihar enacted its own Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.
The Bill seeks time-bound investigation and speedy trial, and doubles debarment of errant service providers to eight years.

prelims.text: Anaemia Mukt Bharat was launched in 2018 with a 6x6x6 strategy: six target groups, six interventions, six institutional mechanisms.
Target groups: children 6-59 months, children 5-9, adolescents 10-19, pregnant women, lactating women, women 15-49.
Interventions include prophylactic IFA, periodic deworming, BCC, digital haemoglobinometer testing and IFA-fortified foods in public programmes.
AMB, under POSHAN Abhiyaan, targets a 3% annual reduction in anaemia.
SAMPADA covered over 2 lakh people in 81,000+ households across 183 districts in 35 States/UTs.
SAMPADA measured haemoglobin by venous blood sampling and automated analysers, the gold-standard method.

mains.text: NFHS-5 found 67.1% of children and 59.1% of adolescent girls anaemic.
SAMPADA analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples; severe anaemia was below 2% in most age groups, with most cases mild.
Anaemia fell by less than 1% a year between 2005 and 2015, prompting the AMB strategy.
15.4 crore children and adolescents received IFA supplements in Q2 of FY 2024-25.
A SAMPADA sub-sample measured iron, folate and vitamin B12; use such biomarkers to target non-iron causes.

prelims.text: The CAQM in NCR and Adjoining Areas Act, 2021 (No. 29 of 2021) was enacted on 12 August 2021.
CAQM coordinates action by Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh on NCR air quality.
Section 12 empowers CAQM to issue directions binding on any person, officer or authority.
PM E-DRIVE was notified by the Ministry of Heavy Industries on 29 September 2024 with a ₹10,900 crore outlay.
PM E-DRIVE earmarks ₹2,000 crore for about 72,000 public EV charging stations.
Setting up EV charging stations is an unlicensed activity open to any entity.

mains.text: CAQM can restrict activities affecting air quality, investigate pollution and prepare codes and guidelines.
PM E-DRIVE plans 22,100 fast chargers for e-4Ws, 1,800 for e-buses and 48,400 for e-2Ws/3Ws.
Outlay rose to ₹11,900 crore with the scheme extended to March 2028; 26.59 lakh EVs sold by June 2026.
Chargers on government premises with free public access get 100% subsidy on upstream infrastructure and equipment.
BHEL is to aggregate demand and develop a unified EV super app for charging.

prelims.text: NSO (MoSPI) has run the Periodic Labour Force Survey since 2017 to estimate employment and unemployment.
From January 2025, PLFS gives monthly LFPR, WPR and UR in CWS for rural and urban areas at all-India level.
The revamp extended quarterly PLFS results to rural areas.
Usual status (ps+ss) uses the last 365 days; CWS uses the last 7 days before the survey.
Usual-status unemployment (15+) fell from 6.0% in 2017-18 to 3.2% in 2023-24.

mains.text: Monthly CWS unemployment (15+) was 5.1% in August and 5.2% in September 2025; urban 6.7% and 6.8%.
Unemployment among the educated (secondary and above) fell to 6.5% in 2025 from 7.0% in 2024.
The old design gave quarterly CWS estimates for urban areas only, with annual estimates for both.
MoSPI now releases all-India indicators monthly and quarterly results for rural, urban and combined areas.

prelims.text: M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India (21 March 2024): SC recognised a right against adverse effects of climate change under Articles 14 and 21.
The Ranjitsinh case concerned protecting the Great Indian Bustard from extinction.
The NAPCC has eight core missions, from solar energy to strategic knowledge for climate change.
33 States and UTs have prepared State Action Plans on Climate Change consistent with NAPCC.
Section 15 of the NGT Act, 2010 lets the Tribunal award relief and compensation to pollution victims and order restitution.
NGT applies sustainable development, precautionary and polluter pays principles in its orders.

mains.text: The SC has held that courts can award damages both to restore ecology and to victims when environmental harm violates Article 21.
NGT, citing Ranjitsinh, called the rights to clean environment and against climate change two sides of the same coin.
The Centre asked States to revise SAPCCs in line with NDC commitments; six States had submitted revised plans.
Ranjitsinh stresses India's international obligations to cut emissions and adapt; States need climate-risk assessments and funds.

prelims.text: The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 came into force in most States/UTs from 1 April 1970.
The RBD (Amendment) Act, 2023 (No. 20 of 2023) came into force on 1 October 2023.
A birth certificate is the single document to prove date and place of birth for those born on or after 1 October 2023.
Births and deaths must be reported within 21 days; certificates are then free.
The Registrar must issue the certificate within seven days of registration, electronically or otherwise.
Registration of births and deaths is in the Concurrent List.

mains.text: Birth certificates prove date and place of birth for school admission, voter lists and government jobs.
Chief Registrars must keep a unified State database of births and deaths on the RGI-approved portal.
Hospitals must report births, with Aadhaar numbers of parents and informant where available.
PRS flagged that mandating birth certificates for these purposes may violate the Constitution.
A further RBD (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (Bill No. 140 of 2026) seeks to amend section 13.

prelims.text: The Indian Space Policy 2023 lets non-government entities take part across the entire space value chain.
IN-SPACe is the autonomous single-window agency to authorise and promote space activities of government entities and NGEs.
FDI: up to 74% automatic in satellite manufacturing and operations, 49% in launch vehicles and spaceports, 100% in components.
NSIL is the commercial arm in the opened-up space sector.
India's space start-ups grew from one in 2014 to over 400 in 2026.

mains.text: Investment in Indian space start-ups rose from US$100.5 million in 2021-22 to US$618.5 million by 31 March 2026.
ISRO launched 399 foreign satellites between 2014 and January 2026.
Skyroot's Vikram-1 is India's first privately developed orbital rocket.
IN-SPACe gives private players access to ISRO launch pads, testing facilities and expertise.
Keep public-sector leadership while encouraging private innovation, investment and entrepreneurship across the space value chain.
